revisit_notes: Parametrized far-field plume model (P ~ F/r^2 with core-peaking kappa and backflow ratio beta), NOT DSMC. Absolute pressures could shift with a real rarefied-plume sim, but H1's 3.6-order margin is robust to any plausible kappa; the geometry-conditioned H2/H4 conclusion (core vs backflow) is the physics, not the exact Pa.

P_damage = 10 kPa is the aerogel compressive limit (conservative); Vectran laminate is ~1000x stronger, so aerogel is correctly the binding surface. If the aerogel intake is stowed/retracted during the dump, even the core case is mechanically safe -- a possible operational mitigation.

H2 stress corner (2.98 N.m, backflow at r=2 m, beta=3e-2, F=10) marginally exceeds the 2.5 N.m threshold: at the closest standoff with the highest backflow ratio the plume is NOT negligible. Standoff >= 3 m (grapple-boom length) keeps it clear. This makes boom length a real design parameter.

Sticking coefficient = 1 (worst-case cold-surface deposition). If the bag surface is above the water frost point during the dump, deposition ~0 and H3 is even safer; if in deep Saturn shadow (~90 K) sticking ~1 holds.

The worst-case-dump-axis question (can a backflow placement always be found?) is answered qualitatively (12 corner thrusters give broad coverage) not by a full attitude-geometry sweep. That sweep is the named follow-on; until then the residual worst-axis risk is exactly what legs C/B exist to retire.

verdict.summary: Plume is NOT a mechanical or contamination showstopper: pressure is 3.6 orders below the aerogel limit (H1) and cumulative intake ice is grams over 50 berths (H3), both robust. The live constraint is RE-PERTURBATION and it is GEOMETRY-CONDITIONED (H2): with the bag in the plume backflow (standoff >= 3 m, tangential-couple thrusters) the torque is ~0.2 N.m, 1/250th of the dump; but if a dump axis forces the bag into the plume core the torque reaches ~22% of the dump and re-excites the just-settled slosh. Verdict: leg A (thruster dump) is VIABLE under a thruster-placement / boom-length constraint (bag in backflow, standoff >= 3 m), which the 12-corner layout can meet for the dump axes -- so the CMG (leg B) and precision-capture (leg C) drop from MANDATORY to OPTIONAL risk reduction for the worst-case-axis residual. The trade does not fully collapse -- it resolves to 'fire the thrusters, place them for backflow, keep boom >= 3 m; hold C/B as the worst-axis backstop.'
